Q: Wireshark Student - I can't see any http post or get requests A:

Capture sample looks like it's filtered, since it contains only packets sent to your PC IP address. What is missing:

  • There is not a single outgoing packet, despite they are obviously on the net. E.g. there are "TCP acknowledge" packets received by PC in capture file, but packets sent by PC, which are acknowledged by them, aren't shown.
  • Not a single incoming broadcast/multicast packet. This situation is possible, but not very likely.

So there is some trouble with sniffer setup on your site. Possible explanations:

  1. accidentally configured capture filter (don't mix with display filter)
  2. Some interfering software is installed. Example of the same complaint

Method to determine if issue is gone: apply !(ip.dst == YOUR_IP_ADDR) display filter and check if packets output isn't empty on visiting any web page. Possible plan of troubleshooting:

  1. check capture filter
  2. check different network card (e.g. non-wireless connection)
  3. check wireshark operability in pure environment (e.g. liveUSB)
  4. try removing suspected interfering software

Q: Invocation of init method failed; nested exception is org.apache.cxf.service.factory.ServiceConstructionException A:

Your main error is 

org.apache.cxf.BusException: No binding factory for namespace http://apache.org/cxf/binding/jaxrs registered.

This related question might help you find a solution: CXF JAX-RS is causing BusException

Q: Reuse Github Actions self hosted runner on multiple repositories A:

Update:

This is possible as of 22nd of April 2020. You can now share runners across an organization. This allows for repositories within your organization to use those runners.

https://github.blog/2020-04-22-github-actions-community-momentum-enterprise-capabilities-and-developer-improvements/#share-self-hosted-runners-across-an-organization

Old Answer:

This is not possible as of yet, according to a Github Partner:

Currently, we have no methods to use the self-hosted runners across repositories, and also have no options to added self-hosted runners on Organization level.

Source: https://github.community/t5/GitHub-Actions/Can-one-Github-Actions-self-hosted-runner-work-for-multiple/td-p/41465

Q: Why is only one of my tasks being cancelled in my python asyncio program? A:

The behaviour comes from two separate issues: how KeyboardInterrupt is handled by asyncio.run() and how your coroutine handles cancellation.

KeyboardInterrupt does not interrupt individual asyncio tasks. It is delivered to the event loop's main execution, causing the main task created by asyncio.run(main()) to be cancelled. That cancellation propagates to the tasks created inside main() (task1, task2, and task3), which receive an asyncio.CancelledError at their next cancellation point.

However, your coro() function only catches:

except Exception:

and asyncio.CancelledError is not caught by that block. It inherits directly from BaseException, not Exception, so normal exception handling will not catch it.

The reason task1 appears to behave differently is because of this line:

time.sleep(1)

time.sleep() blocks the entire event loop. While task1 is sleeping, no other asyncio task can run. The task that happens to be executing when Ctrl+C is pressed receives the interrupt first, and the timing makes it look like only task1 is affected.

The other important detail is:

await asyncio.sleep(0)

This is the point where your coroutine gives control back to the event loop. Cancellation is only delivered when the coroutine reaches an await point. If a task is stuck inside time.sleep(), it cannot immediately receive CancelledError.

A better version would avoid blocking the event loop:

async def coro(id):
    try:
        while True:
            print(f'coro {id} doing something')
            await asyncio.sleep(1)
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        print(f'coro {id} cancelled')
        raise

Now when KeyboardInterrupt occurs, all tasks will receive cancellation cleanly:

coro 1 cancelled
coro 2 cancelled
coro 3 cancelled

In asyncio, tasks are cooperative. They are not separate threads or processes, so they cannot be forcefully interrupted at arbitrary points. They must reach an await where the event loop can inject the CancelledError.
